claims.source: Thapsigargin evoked SOCE in these differentiated neurons; and expression of IP3R1-shRNA significantly reduced the SOCE response without affecting depolarization-evoked Ca2+ signals (Figure 1H–J and Figure 1—figure supplement 1H–L).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 1H–J and Figure 1—figure supplement 1H–L.

claims.claim: SH-SY5Y cells are derived from a human neuroblastoma and exhibit many neuronal characteristics.
claims.source: These cells are derived from a human neuroblastoma; they exhibit many neuronal characteristics (Agholme et al., 2010); they express M3 muscarinic acetylcholine receptors that evoke IP3-mediated Ca2+ release and SOCE (Grudt et al., 1996); and they express predominantly IP3R1 (Wojcikiewicz, 1995; Tovey et al., 2001), with detectable IP3R3, but no IP3R2 (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claims.claim: SH-SY5Y cells express M3 muscarinic acetylcholine receptors that evoke IP3-mediated Ca2+ release and SOCE.
claims.source: These cells are derived from a human neuroblastoma; they exhibit many neuronal characteristics (Agholme et al., 2010); they express M3 muscarinic acetylcholine receptors that evoke IP3-mediated Ca2+ release and SOCE (Grudt et al., 1996); and they express predominantly IP3R1 (Wojcikiewicz, 1995; Tovey et al., 2001), with detectable IP3R3, but no IP3R2 (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claims.claim: SH-SY5Y cells express predominantly IP3R1, with detectable IP3R3, but no IP3R2.
claims.source: These cells are derived from a human neuroblastoma; they exhibit many neuronal characteristics (Agholme et al., 2010); they express M3 muscarinic acetylcholine receptors that evoke IP3-mediated Ca2+ release and SOCE (Grudt et al., 1996); and they express predominantly IP3R1 (Wojcikiewicz, 1995; Tovey et al., 2001), with detectable IP3R3, but no IP3R2 (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2A and citations to the literature.

claims.claim: Inducible expression of IP3R1-shRNA significantly reduced IP3R1 expression by 74 ± 1.2% in SH-SY5Y cells without affecting IP3R3.
claims.source: We used inducible expression of IP3R1-shRNA to significantly reduce IP3R1 expression (by 74 ± 1.2%), without affecting IP3R3 (Figure 2A and B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claims.claim: Carbachol-evoked Ca2+ release was significantly reduced by knockdown of IP3R1 in SH-SY5Y cells.
claims.source: As expected, carbachol-evoked Ca2+ signals in individual SH-SY5Y cells were heterogenous and the carbachol-evoked Ca2+ release was significantly reduced by knockdown of IP3R1 (Figure 2C and D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claims.claim: Thapsigargin-evoked SOCE was significantly attenuated after knockdown of IP3R1 in SH-SY5Y cells without affecting resting [Ca2+]c, the Ca2+ release evoked by thapsigargin or expression of STIM1 and Orai1.
claims.source: Thapsigargin evoked SOCE in SH-SY5Y cells (Grudt et al., 1996), and it was significantly attenuated after knockdown of IP3R1 without affecting resting [Ca2+]c, the Ca2+ release evoked by thapsigargin or expression of STIM1 and Orai1 (Figure 2E–G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging and Western blot data shown in Figure 2E–G and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–E.

claims.claim: CRISPR/Cas9n and Cas9 were used to disrupt one or both copies of the IP3R1 gene in SH-SY5Y cells.
claims.source: We also used CRISPR/Cas9n and Cas9 to disrupt one or both copies of the IP3R1 gene, subsequently referred to as IKO (one copy knockout) and IKO null (both copies knocked out) in SH-SY5Y cells.
claims.evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the experimental approach.

claims.claim: IP3R1 expression was absent in the IKO null SH-SY5Y cells.
claims.source: IP3R1 expression was absent in the IKO null (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F) whereas expression of STIM1, STIM2 and Orai1 were unperturbed (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: Expression of STIM1, STIM2 and Orai1 were unperturbed in IKO null SH-SY5Y cells.
claims.source: IP3R1 expression was absent in the IKO null (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F) whereas expression of STIM1, STIM2 and Orai1 were unperturbed (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claims.claim: Carbachol-evoked Ca2+ release and thapsigargin-evoked SOCE were significantly reduced in IKO null SH-SY5Y cells.
claims.source: Carbachol-evoked Ca2+ release and thapisgargin-evoked SOCE were significantly reduced (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H–J).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H–J.

claims.claim: In IKO SH-SY5Y cells, IP3R1 expression, carbachol-evoked Ca2+ signals and thapsigargin-evoked SOCE were all reduced.
claims.source: In the IKO cells, IP3R1 expression, carbachol-evoked Ca2+ signals and thapsigargin-evoked SOCE were all reduced (Figure 2—figure supplement 1K–Q).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot and calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1K–Q.

claims.claim: Expression of IP3R1 or IP3R3 in SH-SY5Y cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA restored both carbachol-evoked Ca2+ release and thapsigargin-evoked SOCE without affecting resting [Ca2+]c or thapsigargin-evoked Ca2+ release.
claims.source: Expression of IP3R1 or IP3R3 in SH-SY5Y cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA restored both carbachol-evoked Ca2+ release and thapsigargin-evoked SOCE without affecting resting [Ca2+]c or thapsigargin-evoked Ca2+ release (Figure 2H–J and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2H–J and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D.

claims.claim: Over-expression of STIM1 in cells expressing NS-shRNA had no effect on SOCE.
claims.source: Over-expression of STIM1 in cells expressing NS-shRNA had no effect on SOCE (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E and F), but it restored thapsigargin-evoked SOCE in cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA, without affecting resting [Ca2+]c or thapsigargin-evoked Ca2+ release (Figure 2K–M).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E and F.

claims.claim: Over-expression of STIM1 restored thapsigargin-evoked SOCE in cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA, without affecting resting [Ca2+]c or thapsigargin-evoked Ca2+ release.
claims.source: Over-expression of STIM1 in cells expressing NS-shRNA had no effect on SOCE (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E and F), but it restored thapsigargin-evoked SOCE in cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA, without affecting resting [Ca2+]c or thapsigargin-evoked Ca2+ release (Figure 2K–M).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 2K–M.

claims.claim: IP3Rs are required for optimal SOCE, but they are not essential because additional STIM1 can replace the need for IP3Rs.
claims.source: We conclude that IP3Rs are required for optimal SOCE, but they are not essential because additional STIM1 can replace the need for IP3Rs (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing STIM1 overexpression can rescue SOCE in IP3R1-depleted cells.

claims.claim: Expression of IP3R1DA (pore-dead mutant) in cells lacking IP3R1 failed to rescue carbachol-evoked Ca2+ release, but unexpectedly restored thapsigargin-evoked SOCE.
claims.source: As expected, expression of IP3R1D/A in cells lacking IP3R1 failed to rescue carbachol-evoked Ca2+ release, but it unexpectedly restored thapsigargin-evoked SOCE (Figure 3B-D; and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 3B-D.

claims.claim: Rescue of thapsigargin-evoked Ca2+ entry by pore-dead IP3R was mediated by a conventional SOCE pathway as demonstrated by substantial attenuation by siRNA-mediated knockdown of Orai1.
claims.source: We confirmed that rescue of thapsigargin-evoked Ca2+ entry by this pore-dead IP3R was mediated by a conventional SOCE pathway by demonstrating that it was substantially attenuated by siRNA-mediated knockdown of Orai1 (Figure 3C and D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F–H).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 3C and D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F–H.

claims.claim: Mutation of two conserved phosphate-coordinating residues in the α-domain of the IP3-binding core (R568Q and K569Q of IP3R1, IP3R1RQ/KQ) almost abolishes IP3 binding.
claims.source: Mutation of two conserved phosphate-coordinating residues in the α-domain of the binding core (R568Q and K569Q of IP3R1, IP3R1RQ/KQ) almost abolishes IP3 binding (Yoshikawa et al., 1996; Iwai et al., 2007), while mutation of a single residue (R568Q, IP3R1RQ) reduces the IP3 affinity by ~10-fold (Dellis et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to the literature.

claims.claim: Mutation of a single residue (R568Q, IP3R1RQ) reduces the IP3 affinity by ~10-fold.
claims.source: Mutation of two conserved phosphate-coordinating residues in the α-domain of the binding core (R568Q and K569Q of IP3R1, IP3R1RQ/KQ) almost abolishes IP3 binding (Yoshikawa et al., 1996; Iwai et al., 2007), while mutation of a single residue (R568Q, IP3R1RQ) reduces the IP3 affinity by ~10-fold (Dellis et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to the literature.

claims.claim: Expression of rat IP3R1RQ/KQ rescued neither carbachol-evoked Ca2+ release nor thapsigargin-evoked SOCE in cells lacking IP3R1.
claims.source: Expression of rat IP3R1RQ/KQ rescued neither carbachol-evoked Ca2+ release nor thapsigargin-evoked SOCE in cells lacking IP3R1 (Figure 3E and F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and I).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 3E and F.

claims.claim: Expression of IP3R1RQ substantially rescued thapsigargin-evoked SOCE.
claims.source: However, expression of IP3R1RQ substantially rescued thapsigargin-evoked SOCE (Figure 3E and F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1J).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 3E and F.

claims.claim: Expression of an N-terminal fragment of rat IP3R (IP3R11-604), to which IP3 binds normally, failed to rescue thapsigargin-evoked SOCE.
claims.source: Expression of an N-terminal fragment of rat IP3R (IP3R11-604), to which IP3 binds normally (Iwai et al., 2007), failed to rescue thapsigargin-evoked SOCE (Figure 3—figure supplement 1K and L).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1K and L.

claims.claim: A functional IP3-binding site within a full-length IP3R is required for IP3Rs to facilitate thapsigargin-evoked SOCE.
claims.source: These results establish that a functional IP3-binding site within a full-length IP3R is required for IP3Rs to facilitate thapsigargin-evoked SOCE.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data with IP3R mutants.

claims.claim: In cells with empty Ca2+ stores, IP3 binding, but not pore-opening, is required for regulation of SOCE by IP3Rs.
claims.source: Hence in cells with empty Ca2+ stores, IP3 binding, but not pore-opening, is required for regulation of SOCE by IP3Rs.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data with pore-dead and ligand-binding mutants.

claims.claim: Addition of carbachol to SH-SY5Y cells expressing IP3R1DA with partially depleted ER Ca2+ stores substantially increased SOCE from sub maximal to higher levels.
claims.source: The key result is that in cells expressing IP3R1DA, carbachol substantially increased SOCE from sub maximal to higher levels (Figure 4AC).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claims.claim: Addition of carbachol to control shRNA expressing SH-SY5Y cells with maximal store depletion resulted in a small increase in SOCE.
claims.source: Moreover, addition of carbachol to control shRNA expressing SH-SY5Y cells with maximal store depletion (thapsigargin, Tg, 2 µM) resulted in a small increase in SOCE (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: In neuronal cells IP3, through IP3Rs, regulates coupling of empty stores to SOCE.
claims.source: We conclude that in neuronal cells IP3, through IP3Rs, regulates coupling of empty stores to SOCE.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing IP3 enhances SOCE.

claims.claim: This is the first example of an IP3R mediating a response to IP3 that does not require the pore of the channel.
claims.source: This is the first example of an IP3R mediating a response to IP3 that does not require the pore of the channel.
claims.evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding, based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claims.claim: YM-254890 inhibits Gq.
claims.source: We used YM-254890 to inhibit Gq (Kostenis et al., 2020; Patt et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: Addition of YM-254890 to wild type or NS-shRNA transfected SH-SY5Y cells abolished the Ca2+ signals evoked by carbachol.
claims.source: As expected, addition of YM-254890 to wild type (WT) or NS-shRNA transfected SH-SY5Y cells abolished the Ca2+ signals evoked by carbachol (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), but it also reduced the maximal amplitude and rate of thapsigargin-evoked SOCE (Figure 4D–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1O).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: YM-254890 reduced the maximal amplitude and rate of thapsigargin-evoked SOCE in wild type or NS-shRNA transfected SH-SY5Y cells.
claims.source: As expected, addition of YM-254890 to wild type (WT) or NS-shRNA transfected SH-SY5Y cells abolished the Ca2+ signals evoked by carbachol (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), but it also reduced the maximal amplitude and rate of thapsigargin-evoked SOCE (Figure 4D–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1O).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4D–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1O.

claims.claim: YM-254890 had no effect on the residual thapsigargin-evoked SOCE in SH-SY5Y cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA.
claims.source: YM-254890 had no effect on the residual thapsigargin-evoked SOCE in SH-SY5Y cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA (Figure 4F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1O).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1O.

claims.claim: The inhibition of SOCE by YM-254890 in cells with functional IP3Rs is not an off-target effect causing a direct inhibition of SOCE.
claims.source: The latter result is important because it demonstrates that the inhibition of SOCE in cells with functional IP3Rs is not an off-target effect causing a direct inhibition of SOCE.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing selective effects of YM-254890.

claims.claim: In wild type or HEK-TKO cells, YM-254890 had no effect on thapsigargin-evoked SOCE.
claims.source: In wild type or HEK-TKO (lacking all three IP3Rs) cells, YM-254890 had no effect on thapsigargin-evoked SOCE, but it did inhibit SOCE in HEK cells lacking only IP3R1 (Figure 4G–I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4G–I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–G.

claims.claim: YM-254890 inhibited SOCE in HEK cells lacking only IP3R1.
claims.source: In wild type or HEK-TKO (lacking all three IP3Rs) cells, YM-254890 had no effect on thapsigargin-evoked SOCE, but it did inhibit SOCE in HEK cells lacking only IP3R1 (Figure 4G–I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4G–I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–G.

claims.claim: In HEK cells, which normally express all three IP3R subtypes, neither loss of IP3R1 nor inhibition of Gαq is sufficient on its own to inhibit thapsigargin-evoked SOCE, but when combined there is a synergistic loss of SOCE.
claims.source: These results suggest that in HEK cells, which normally express all three IP3R subtypes (Mataragka and Taylor, 2018), neither loss of IP3R1 nor inhibition of Gαq is sufficient on its own to inhibit thapsigargin-evoked SOCE, but when combined there is a synergistic loss of SOCE.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data with HEK cells.

claims.claim: A proximity ligation assay (PLA) provides a signal when two immunolabeled proteins are within ~40 nm of each other.
claims.source: An in situ proximity ligation assay (PLA) is well suited to analyzing this interaction because it provides a signal when two immunolabeled proteins are within ~40 nm of each other (Derangère et al., 2016), a distance comparable to the dimensions of the junctions wherein STIM1 and Orai1 interact (Poteser et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about the PLA technique, supported by citations.

claims.claim: PLA reports increased association of STIM1 with Orai1 after treating SH-SY5Y cells with thapsigargin.
claims.source: We confirmed the specificity of the PLA and demonstrated that it reports increased association of STIM1 with Orai1 after treating SH-SY5Y cells with thapsigargin by measuring the surface area of PLA spots (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–F) and not the number, because the latter did not change upon store-depletion (Figure 5—figure supplement 1O).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PLA data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–F.

claims.claim: In cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA, thapsigargin had no effect on the STIM1-Orai1 interaction reported by PLA.
claims.source: In cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA, thapsigargin had no effect on the STIM1-Orai1 interaction reported by PLA, but the interaction was rescued by expression of IP3R1 or IP3R1DA.
claims.evidence: This is supported by PLA data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: The STIM1-Orai1 interaction in cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA was rescued by expression of IP3R1 or IP3R1DA.
claims.source: In cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA, thapsigargin had no effect on the STIM1-Orai1 interaction reported by PLA, but the interaction was rescued by expression of IP3R1 or IP3R1DA.
claims.evidence: This is supported by PLA data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claims.claim: There was no rescue of STIM1-Orai1 interaction with IP3R1RQ/KQ.
claims.source: There was no rescue with IP3R1RQ/KQ (Figure 5B–E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PLA data shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: WT SH-SY5Y cells that were depleted of basal IP3 by treatment with the Gq inhibitor YM-254890, showed significantly reduced STIM1-Orai1 interaction after thapsigargin-evoked depletion of Ca2+ stores.
claims.source: WT SH-SY5Y cells that were depleted of basal IP3 by treatment with the Gq inhibitor YM-254890, showed significantly reduced STIM1-Orai1 interaction after thapsigargin-evoked depletion of Ca2+ stores (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PLA data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: IP3 binding to IP3R enhances SOCE by facilitating interaction of STIM1 with Orai1.
claims.source: The results with PLA exactly mirror those from functional analyses (Figures 1—4), suggesting that IP3 binding to IP3R enhances SOCE by facilitating interaction of STIM1 with Orai1 (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the convergence of PLA and functional data.

claims.claim: ER-PM translocation of mVenus-STIM1 upon SOCE induction was reduced significantly in mCherry-IP3R1RQ/KQ expressing cells compared to mCherry-IP3R1 expressing SH-SY5Y cells.
claims.source: In agreement with PLA data (Figure 5), ER-PM translocation of mVenus-STIM1 upon SOCE induction was reduced significantly in mCherry-IP3R1RQ/KQ expressing cells compared to mCherry-IP3R1 expressing SH-SY5Y cells (Figure 6A, B, D and E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 6A, B, D and E.

claims.claim: SOCE brought about a small increase in the surface intensity of over-expressed wild type mCherry-IP3R1 and mCherry-IP3R1RQ/KQ in the regions where SOCE-dependent STIM1 puncta form.
claims.source: SOCE also brought about a small increase in the surface intensity of over-expressed wild type mCherry-IP3R1 and mCherry-IP3R1RQ/KQ in the regions where we observe formation of SOCE-dependent STIM1 puncta (Figure 6A–C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TIRF microscopy data shown in Figure 6A–C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and E.

claims.claim: Over-expression of E-Syt1 in SH-SY5Y cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA rescued thapsigargin-evoked Ca2+ entry without affecting resting [Ca2+]c or thapsigargin-evoked Ca2+ release.
claims.source: Over-expression of E-Syt1 in SH-SY5Y cells expressing IP3R1-shRNA rescued thapsigargin-evoked Ca2+ entry without affecting resting [Ca2+]c or thapsigargin-evoked Ca2+ release (Figure 7A–C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 7A–C.

claims.claim: The rescued Ca2+ entry by E-Syt1 overexpression is likely to be mediated by conventional SOCE because it was substantially attenuated by knockdown of STIM1.
claims.source: The rescued Ca2+ entry is likely to be mediated by conventional SOCE because it was substantially attenuated by knockdown of STIM1 (Figure 7D–F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 7D–F.

claims.claim: Over-expression of E-Syt1 had no effect on SOCE in cells with unperturbed IP3Rs.
claims.source: Over-expression of E-Syt1 had no effect on SOCE in cells with unperturbed IP3Rs (Figure 7G–I).
claims.evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 7G–I.

claims.claim: Attenuated SOCE after loss of IP3Rs can be restored by exaggerating ER-PM MCS.
claims.source: These results suggest that attenuated SOCE after loss of IP3Rs can be restored by exaggerating ER-PM MCS.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the E-Syt1 overexpression experiments.

claims.claim: After identification of STIM1 and Orai1 as core components of SOCE, the sole role of IP3Rs within the SOCE pathway was assumed to be the release of ER Ca2+ that triggers STIM1 activation.
claims.source: After identification of STIM1 and Orai1 as core components of SOCE (Prakriya and Lewis, 2015; Thillaiappan et al., 2019), the sole role of IP3Rs within the SOCE pathway was assumed to be the release of ER Ca2+ that triggers STIM1 activation.
claims.evidence: This is presented as the prevailing assumption in the field, supported by citations.

claims.claim: Thapsigargin-evoked SOCE can occur in avian and mammalian cells without IP3Rs.
claims.source: The assumption is consistent with evidence that thapsigargin-evoked SOCE can occur in avian (Sugawara et al., 1997; Ma et al., 2002; Chakraborty et al., 2016) and mammalian cells without IP3Rs (Prakriya and Lewis, 2001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claims.claim: SOCE in mammalian HEK cells was unaffected by loss of IP3Rs in this study.
claims.source: Although SOCE in mammalian HEK cells was unaffected by loss of IP3Rs in our study (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), it was modestly reduced in other studies of mammalian cells (Bartok et al., 2019; Yue et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: SOCE was modestly reduced in other studies of mammalian cells without IP3Rs.
claims.source: Although SOCE in mammalian HEK cells was unaffected by loss of IP3Rs in our study (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), it was modestly reduced in other studies of mammalian cells (Bartok et al., 2019; Yue et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to other studies.

claims.claim: There is evidence that SOCE may be reduced in cells without IP3Rs.
claims.source: However, additional complexity is suggested by evidence that SOCE may be reduced in cells without IP3Rs (Chakraborty et al., 2016; Bartok et al., 2019; Yue et al., 2020), by observations implicating phospholipase C in SOCE regulation (Rosado et al., 2000; Broad et al., 2001), by evidence that SOCE responds differently to IP3Rs activated by different synthetic ligands (Parekh et al., 2002) and by some, albeit conflicting reports (Woodard et al., 2010; Santoso et al., 2011; Béliveau et al., 2014; Sampieri et al., 2018; Ahmad et al., 2022), that IP3Rs may interact with STIM and/or Orai (Woodard et al., 2010; Santoso et al., 2011; Béliveau et al., 2014; Sampieri et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claims.claim: There are observations implicating phospholipase C in SOCE regulation.
claims.source: However, additional complexity is suggested by evidence that SOCE may be reduced in cells without IP3Rs (Chakraborty et al., 2016; Bartok et al., 2019; Yue et al., 2020), by observations implicating phospholipase C in SOCE regulation (Rosado et al., 2000; Broad et al., 2001), by evidence that SOCE responds differently to IP3Rs activated by different synthetic ligands (Parekh et al., 2002) and by some, albeit conflicting reports (Woodard et al., 2010; Santoso et al., 2011; Béliveau et al., 2014; Sampieri et al., 2018; Ahmad et al., 2022), that IP3Rs may interact with STIM and/or Orai (Woodard et al., 2010; Santoso et al., 2011; Béliveau et al., 2014; Sampieri et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claims.claim: There is evidence that SOCE responds differently to IP3Rs activated by different synthetic ligands.
claims.source: However, additional complexity is suggested by evidence that SOCE may be reduced in cells without IP3Rs (Chakraborty et al., 2016; Bartok et al., 2019; Yue et al., 2020), by observations implicating phospholipase C in SOCE regulation (Rosado et al., 2000; Broad et al., 2001), by evidence that SOCE responds differently to IP3Rs activated by different synthetic ligands (Parekh et al., 2002) and by some, albeit conflicting reports (Woodard et al., 2010; Santoso et al., 2011; Béliveau et al., 2014; Sampieri et al., 2018; Ahmad et al., 2022), that IP3Rs may interact with STIM and/or Orai (Woodard et al., 2010; Santoso et al., 2011; Béliveau et al., 2014; Sampieri et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claims.claim: There are some, albeit conflicting reports, that IP3Rs may interact with STIM and/or Orai.
claims.source: However, additional complexity is suggested by evidence that SOCE may be reduced in cells without IP3Rs (Chakraborty et al., 2016; Bartok et al., 2019; Yue et al., 2020), by observations implicating phospholipase C in SOCE regulation (Rosado et al., 2000; Broad et al., 2001), by evidence that SOCE responds differently to IP3Rs activated by different synthetic ligands (Parekh et al., 2002) and by some, albeit conflicting reports (Woodard et al., 2010; Santoso et al., 2011; Béliveau et al., 2014; Sampieri et al., 2018; Ahmad et al., 2022), that IP3Rs may interact with STIM and/or Orai (Woodard et al., 2010; Santoso et al., 2011; Béliveau et al., 2014; Sampieri et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claims.claim: IP3Rs have two roles in controlling endogenous SOCE in human neurons: activating STIM1 by releasing Ca2+ from the ER, and enhancing interactions between active STIM1 and Orai1 independent of their ability to release Ca2+.
claims.source: We identified two roles for IP3Rs in controlling endogenous SOCE in human neurons. As widely reported, IP3Rs activate STIM1 by releasing Ca2+ from the ER, but they also, and independent of their ability to release Ca2+, enhance interactions between active STIM1 and Orai1 (Figure 8).
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claims.claim: The second role for IP3Rs can be supplanted by over-expressing other components of the SOCE complex, notably STIM1 or ESyt1.
claims.source: The second role for IP3Rs can be supplanted by over-expressing other components of the SOCE complex, notably STIM1 or ESyt1 (Figure 2K–M and Figure 7A and B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2K–M and Figure 7A and B.

claims.claim: STIM1, ESyt1 and perhaps IP3Rs interact with phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2), which is dynamically associated with SOCE-MCS.
claims.source: It is intriguing that STIM1 (Carrasco and Meyer, 2011; Lewis, 2020), ESyt1 (Giordano et al., 2013) and perhaps IP3Rs (through the IP3-binding core) interact with phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2), which is dynamically associated with SOCE-MCS (Kang et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claims.claim: The extent to which IP3Rs tune SOCE in different cells is probably determined by the strength of Gq signaling, the proximity of IP3Rs to nanodomains of PLC signaling and endogenous interactions between STIM1 and Orai1.
claims.source: We suggest that the extent to which IP3Rs tune SOCE in different cells is probably determined by the strength of Gq signaling, the proximity of IP3Rs to nanodomains of PLC signaling and endogenous interactions between STIM1 and Orai1.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claims.claim: Endogenous interactions between STIM1 and Orai1 are likely to depend on the relative expression of STIM1 and Orai1, the STIM isoforms expressed, expression of proteins that stabilize STIM1-Orai1 interactions, and the size and number of the MCS where STIM1 and Orai1 interact.

claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations to the literature.

claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4H and I.

claims.source: The persistence of SOCE in cells devoid of IP3Rs (Figure 2—figure supplement 3D and E; Prakriya and Lewis, 2001; Ma et al., 2002) possibly arises from adaptive changes within the SOCE pathway.

claims.source: This does not detract from our conclusion that under physiological conditions, where receptors through IP3 initiate SOCE, IP3Rs actively regulate SOCE.

claims.source: The IP3Rs that initiate Ca2+ signals reside in ER immediately beneath the PM and alongside, but not within, the MCS where STIM1 accumulates after store depletion (Thillaiappan et al., 2017; Figure 6A and B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 6A and B and a citation to the literature.

claims.source: In migrating cells too, IP3Rs and STIM1 remain separated as they redistribute to the leading edge (Okeke et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claims.source: Furthermore, there is evidence that neither STIM1 nor STIM2 co-immmunoprecipitate with IP3R1 (Ahmad et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claims.claim: Ligand-bound IP3Rs facilitate SOCE either by stabilizing the MCS wherein STIM1 and Orai1 interact, or by indirectly supporting STIM1 movement towards the MCS, rather than by directly regulating either protein.
claims.source: We suggest, and consistent with evidence that SOCE in cells without IP3Rs can be restored by over-expressing E-Syt1 (Figure 7A–C), that ligand-bound IP3Rs facilitate SOCE either by stabilizing the MCS wherein STIM1 and Orai1 interact, or by indirectly supporting STIM1 movement towards the MCS, rather than by directly regulating either protein.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings, supported by experimental data.

claims.source: Stabilization of the MCS is analogous with similar structural roles for IP3Rs in maintaining MCS between ER and mitochondria (Bartok et al., 2019) or lysosomes (Atakpa et al., 2018; Figure 8).

claims.source: Convergent regulation by IP3Rs at two steps in the SOCE pathway may ensure that receptor-regulated PLC activity provides the most effective stimulus for SOCE; more effective, for example, than ryanodine receptors, which are also expressed in neurons (Figure 8B).

claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by experimental data.

results.result: Loss of IP3R1 in human neural progenitor cells (hNPCs) and differentiated neurons significantly reduces SOCE amplitude and rate without affecting resting Ca2+ levels, thapsigargin-evoked Ca2+ release, or STIM1/Orai1 expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C31-33, C37, and C43 collectively demonstrate that IP3R1 knockdown attenuates SOCE in hNPCs and neurons while leaving other Ca2+ handling parameters intact. The data from Figures 1 and supplementary figures provide consistent evidence across multiple cell preparations with appropriate controls (resting Ca2+, store content, STIM1/Orai1 expression).

results.result: In SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells, IP3R1 knockdown (shRNA) or knockout (CRISPR) significantly reduces both carbachol-evoked Ca2+ release and thapsigargin-evoked SOCE, which can be rescued by re-expression of IP3R1 or IP3R3.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-43, C47-49 demonstrate consistent attenuation of SOCE with IP3R1 loss using multiple approaches (shRNA, CRISPR IKO, IKO null) and successful rescue with IP3R re-expression. The data from Figure 2 and supplements provide convergent evidence with appropriate controls and rescue experiments.

results.result: Overexpression of STIM1 can restore SOCE in IP3R1-depleted cells without affecting resting Ca2+ or store content, indicating that IP3Rs are required for optimal SOCE but are not absolutely essential.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-52 show that STIM1 overexpression specifically rescues SOCE deficits in IP3R1-depleted cells (Figure 2K-M) without affecting other Ca2+ parameters. This demonstrates that the SOCE pathway can be restored by increasing STIM1 levels, supporting the conclusion that IP3Rs facilitate but are not absolutely required for SOCE.

results.result: A pore-dead IP3R1 mutant (IP3R1D/A) that cannot release Ca2+ can still rescue SOCE in IP3R1-depleted cells, and this rescue requires an intact IP3-binding site, demonstrating that IP3Rs regulate SOCE independent of their Ca2+ release function.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-54, C60-61 establish a critical mechanistic finding: IP3R1D/A rescues SOCE (Figure 3B-D) despite inability to release Ca2+, and this rescue is Orai1-dependent. The requirement for IP3 binding (but not pore function) is demonstrated by experiments with binding-deficient mutants (IP3R1RQ/KQ), providing strong evidence for a non-canonical IP3R function.

results.result: IP3R mutants with severely impaired IP3 binding (IP3R1RQ/KQ) cannot rescue SOCE, while a mutant with moderately reduced affinity (IP3R1RQ) can partially rescue SOCE, and an N-terminal IP3-binding fragment alone is insufficient, demonstrating that full-length IP3R with functional IP3 binding is required.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-59 systematically dissect the structural requirements for IP3R's role in SOCE using mutants with different IP3-binding capacities (Figure 3E-F and supplements). The graded response (no rescue with RQ/KQ, partial with RQ, none with N-terminal fragment) provides strong evidence that IP3 binding to full-length IP3R is necessary for SOCE regulation.

results.result: In cells expressing pore-dead IP3R1, addition of carbachol to stimulate IP3 production substantially increases SOCE from submaximal levels, demonstrating that IP3 regulates SOCE through IP3Rs independent of Ca2+ release—the first example of such IP3R signaling.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-65 demonstrate that IP3 generation (via carbachol) enhances SOCE in cells with pore-dead IP3Rs (Figure 4A-C), proving IP3 can regulate SOCE without triggering Ca2+ release. The use of partial store depletion (CPA) to create submaximal SOCE is appropriate, and the novelty claim (C65) appears justified based on the literature context provided.

results.result: The Gq inhibitor YM-254890 reduces thapsigargin-evoked SOCE in wild-type SH-SY5Y cells but not in IP3R1-depleted cells, demonstrating that basal IP3 production contributes to SOCE in cells with functional IP3Rs and ruling out off-target effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-70 show that YM-254890 selectively inhibits SOCE in cells with functional IP3Rs (Figure 4D-F), with the critical control (C69) showing no effect in IP3R1-depleted cells. This selectivity strongly supports the interpretation that the effect is mediated through IP3/IP3R signaling rather than direct SOCE inhibition.

results.result: In HEK cells expressing all three IP3R subtypes, neither IP3R1 loss nor Gq inhibition alone affects SOCE, but their combination synergistically reduces SOCE, suggesting functional redundancy among IP3R subtypes and IP3 signaling pathways.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-73 demonstrate cell-type-specific differences in IP3R contribution to SOCE (Figure 4G-I). The synergistic effect of combined IP3R1 loss and Gq inhibition in HEK cells (which express all three IP3R subtypes) provides evidence for redundancy, though the inference about mechanism (C73) is reasonable given the data.

results.result: Proximity ligation assays demonstrate that IP3Rs enhance STIM1-Orai1 association after store depletion in a manner requiring IP3 binding but not pore function, as shown by rescue with IP3R1 or pore-dead IP3R1D/A but not with IP3-binding-deficient IP3R1RQ/KQ.
results.evaluation: Claims C75-80 provide imaging evidence that parallels the functional data, showing IP3R-dependent enhancement of STIM1-Orai1 interaction (Figure 5). The PLA results with different IP3R mutants exactly mirror the SOCE functional data, providing strong convergent evidence for the proposed mechanism. However, PLA has only n=2 biological replicates, which is a limitation.

results.result: TIRF microscopy shows that SOCE-induced STIM1 translocation to ER-PM junctions is significantly reduced in cells expressing IP3-binding-deficient IP3R1RQ/KQ compared to wild-type IP3R1, with modest changes in IP3R surface localization.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-82 and C109 provide direct visualization of STIM1 dynamics using TIRF microscopy (Figure 6), showing reduced STIM1 puncta formation with IP3R1RQ/KQ. The authors appropriately note uncertainty about the significance of small changes in IP3R surface intensity, demonstrating appropriate caution in interpretation.

results.result: Overexpression of E-Syt1, which stabilizes ER-PM membrane contact sites, rescues SOCE in IP3R1-depleted cells in a STIM1-dependent manner without affecting cells with intact IP3Rs, suggesting IP3Rs facilitate SOCE by stabilizing or promoting MCS formation.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-86 show that E-Syt1 overexpression can compensate for IP3R loss (Figure 7A-C), with appropriate controls showing STIM1-dependence (C84) and specificity for IP3R-depleted cells (C85). The inference about MCS stabilization (C86) is reasonable given E-Syt1's known function, though the mechanism remains indirect.

results.result: SOCE in HEK cells is unaffected by IP3R loss in this study, though other studies report modest reductions, with the persistence of SOCE in IP3R-null cells possibly arising from adaptive changes in the SOCE pathway.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-91 and C102 acknowledge cell-type differences and literature discrepancies regarding IP3R's role in SOCE. The data from Figure 2—figure supplement 3 support the lack of effect in HEK cells, and the speculation about adaptive changes (C102) is appropriately qualified. This demonstrates scientific rigor in acknowledging conflicting data.

results.result: IP3Rs have dual roles in SOCE regulation: (1) activating STIM1 through Ca2+ release, and (2) facilitating STIM1-Orai1 interactions independent of Ca2+ release, with the second role being supplantable by overexpressing STIM1 or E-Syt1, allowing robust receptor control of Ca2+ entry.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-96, C114-116 synthesize the major findings into a coherent model supported by the collective experimental evidence. The dual-role model is well-supported by the pore-dead mutant experiments, PLA data, and rescue experiments with STIM1/E-Syt1. The speculation about physiological significance (C116) is appropriately qualified.

results.result: In neuronal cells, loss of either IP3 or IP3R1 alone is sufficient to reduce SOCE, whereas HEK cells require loss of both IP3 and IP3R1, indicating cell-type-specific differences in the requirement for IP3R regulation of SOCE.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-101 compare neuronal and non-neuronal cells, showing differential sensitivity to IP3R loss (Figures 1-2 vs. Figure 4H-I). This cell-type specificity is well-documented and likely reflects differences in IP3R subtype expression and/or SOCE component stoichiometry, as discussed by the authors.

results.result: IP3Rs reside in ER adjacent to but not within SOCE-MCS, do not co-immunoprecipitate with STIM1/2, and likely facilitate SOCE by stabilizing MCS or supporting STIM1 movement rather than through direct protein-protein interactions, analogous to IP3R roles at other MCS.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-108 propose mechanisms for how IP3Rs facilitate SOCE without direct STIM1 interaction. While the spatial separation (C104-105) and lack of co-IP (C106) are supported by citations, the mechanistic proposals (C107-108) remain speculative. The E-Syt1 rescue data support MCS involvement, but direct evidence for the proposed mechanisms is lacking.

results.result: Both IP3R contributions to SOCE require IP3 binding, creating convergent regulation whereby IP3 both releases Ca2+ from optimally positioned ER and facilitates STIM1-Orai1 interactions, potentially ensuring that receptor-stimulated IP3 production provides the most effective SOCE stimulus.
results.evaluation: Claims C110-113 integrate the findings into a physiological model where IP3 coordinates both Ca2+ release and SOCE activation. The requirement for IP3 binding in both processes is well-supported experimentally (Figures 3-4), and the proposed functional significance is a reasonable inference, though the comparative advantage over other Ca2+ release mechanisms (e.g., RyR) remains speculative.

results.result: hNPCs express neural stem cell markers and predominantly IP3R1, and after differentiation express neuronal markers and respond to depolarization, validating the cell model system.
results.evaluation: Claims C22-24, C34-35 establish the cellular model with appropriate characterization (Figure 1A and supplements). The immunofluorescence, gene expression, and functional data (depolarization response) provide adequate validation of the hNPC and differentiated neuron phenotypes.

results.result: SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells express neuronal characteristics, M3 muscarinic receptors, and predominantly IP3R1 (with some IP3R3 but no IP3R2), making them suitable for studying IP3R regulation of SOCE in a neuronal context.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-41 justify the use of SH-SY5Y cells as a neuronal model with appropriate characterization (Figure 2A-B and citations). The Western blot data confirm IP3R expression patterns, and the successful knockdown (74% reduction) validates the experimental approach.

results.result: CRISPR/Cas9 and Cas9n were used to generate IP3R1 knockout cell lines (IKO and IKO null) with confirmed loss of IP3R1 expression while maintaining normal STIM1, STIM2, and Orai1 levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-46 describe the generation and validation of CRISPR-edited cell lines (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F-G). The Western blot data confirm successful IP3R1 knockout without affecting SOCE machinery components, providing an important complementary approach to shRNA knockdown.

results.result: In hNPCs, carbachol evokes Ca2+ release in ~10% of cells in Ca2+-free medium, followed by SOCE upon Ca2+ restoration, with both responses abolished by IP3R1 knockdown.
results.evaluation: Claims C26-28 establish that hNPCs respond to muscarinic stimulation with IP3R-dependent Ca2+ signals (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C). The low response rate (~10%) is consistent with low muscarinic receptor expression (C25), and the complete abolition with IP3R1-shRNA validates the knockdown.

results.result: Background on SOCE mechanism and IP3R function: STIM1 senses ER Ca2+ depletion and activates Orai channels at MCS, with IP3Rs traditionally thought to contribute only through Ca2+ release, though additional regulatory proteins and MCS assembly factors are known.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C7-16 provide established background knowledge about SOCE and IP3R biology, appropriately supported by citations. These claims set up the prevailing model (C16) that the authors challenge with their new findings. The background is accurate and well-referenced.

results.result: Thapsigargin irreversibly inhibits SERCA to deplete ER Ca2+ and activate SOCE, while YM-254890 inhibits Gq to block receptor-stimulated IP3 production.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-30 and C66 describe standard pharmacological tools used throughout the study. The mechanisms of action are well-established (supported by citations), and the functional validation is shown in multiple figures (e.g., Figure 1D for thapsigargin, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C for YM-254890).

results.result: Mutations in the IP3-binding core (R568Q/K569Q = IP3R1RQ/KQ) nearly abolish IP3 binding, while single mutation (R568Q = IP3R1RQ) reduces affinity ~10-fold.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-56 describe established properties of IP3R mutants based on prior structural and functional studies (supported by citations to Yoshikawa et al., 1996; Iwai et al., 2007; Dellis et al., 2008). These mutants are appropriately used as tools to dissect IP3-binding requirements.

results.result: Proximity ligation assay (PLA) detects protein interactions within ~40 nm, suitable for analyzing STIM1-Orai1 interactions at MCS.
results.evaluation: Claim C74 describes the PLA technique with appropriate citations (Derangère et al., 2016; Poteser et al., 2016). The ~40 nm detection range is well-matched to MCS dimensions, justifying the methodological choice. The specificity controls are shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

results.result: Prior literature shows complexity in IP3R's role in SOCE: evidence from Drosophila suggested additional IP3R functions, some studies show SOCE reduction without IP3Rs, and conflicting reports exist about IP3R interactions with STIM/Orai, motivating the current study.
results.evaluation: Claims C17, C87-88, C91-94 review prior literature establishing the context and motivation for the study. The citations appropriately acknowledge both supporting evidence (Drosophila studies, C17) and conflicting reports (C94), demonstrating scholarly awareness of the field's complexity.

results.result: STIM1, E-Syt1, and possibly IP3Rs interact with PIP2 at SOCE-MCS, and the extent of IP3R contribution to SOCE likely depends on Gq signaling strength, IP3R proximity to PLC nanodomains, and endogenous STIM1-Orai1 interaction strength, which varies with expression levels and MCS properties.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-99 propose factors determining cell-type-specific IP3R contributions to SOCE. While PIP2 interactions are supported by citations (C97), the proposed determinants of IP3R contribution (C98-99) are largely speculative, though reasonable given the data. These represent testable hypotheses for future work rather than demonstrated findings.

results.result: The authors speculate that dual IP3R regulation may tune neuronal SOCE to respond selectively to IP3-generating receptors under physiological conditions, though this functional significance remains to be directly tested.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C20, and C103 present the authors' speculation about physiological significance. While the dual regulation is well-established experimentally, the proposed selective coupling to IP3-generating receptors (vs. other Ca2+ release mechanisms) remains hypothetical and would require additional experiments to test directly.
